# zhbev

> Computes all eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a complex Hermitian band matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zhbev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zhbev';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zhbev( order, jobz, uplo, N, kd, AB, LDAB, w, strideW, Z, LDZ, WORK, RWORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- (or sub-) diagonals<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Band matrix in band storage |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AB`<br>Column-major requires `LDAB ≥ kd + 1`<br>Row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | `w` stride length |
| `Z` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix for eigenvectors |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Z`<br>Rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Complex workspace array |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 3 * N - 2)</sub> | **out** · Real workspace array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$.

  On exit, `AB` is overwritten by values generated during the reduction to tridiagonal form. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the first superdiagonal and the diagonal of the tridiagonal matrix T are returned in rows `KD` and `KD`+1 of `AB`, and if `UPLO = 'L'`, the diagonal and first subdiagonal of T are returned in the first two rows of `AB`.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, Z contains the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `kd + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zhbev.ndarray(
    jobz, uplo,
    N, kd,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → integer
```

Computes all eigenvalues and optionally eigenvectors of a complex Hermitian band matrix.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- (or sub-) diagonals<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Band matrix in band storage |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AB` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AB` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AB` (in complex elements) |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `w` |
| `Z` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix for eigenvectors |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Z` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Z` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Z` (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Complex workspace array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` (in complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 3 * N - 2)</sub> | **out** · Real workspace array |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `RWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `RWORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$.

  On exit, `AB` is overwritten by values generated during the reduction to tridiagonal form. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the first superdiagonal and the diagonal of the tridiagonal matrix T are returned in rows `KD` and `KD`+1 of `AB`, and if `UPLO = 'L'`, the diagonal and first subdiagonal of T are returned in the first two rows of `AB`.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, Z contains the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit.
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, the algorithm failed to converge; i off-diagonal elements of an intermediate tridiagonal form did not converge to zero.

</section>

## Notes

-   `zhbev()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZHBEV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zhbev.f).

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zhbev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zhbev';

// 4x4 Hermitian tridiagonal (KD=1), lower band, column-major:
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 10 );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 4 );
const AB = new Complex128Array( 2 * 4 );
const ABv = reinterpret( AB, 0 );
const W = new Float64Array( 4 );
const Z = new Complex128Array( 16 );

// Col 1: diag=4, subdiag=(1+i)
ABv[ 0 ] = 4.0;
ABv[ 2 ] = 1.0;
ABv[ 3 ] = 1.0;

// Col 2: diag=5, subdiag=(2-i)
ABv[ 4 ] = 5.0;
ABv[ 6 ] = 2.0;
ABv[ 7 ] = -1.0;

// Col 3: diag=6, subdiag=(3+i)
ABv[ 8 ] = 6.0;
ABv[ 10 ] = 3.0;
ABv[ 11 ] = 1.0;

// Col 4: diag=7
ABv[ 12 ] = 7.0;

const info = zhbev( 'column-major', 'compute-vectors', 'lower', 4, 1, AB, 2, W, 1, Z, 4, WORK, RWORK ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info );       // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Eigenvalues:', W );   // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>
